options.C: Net income flows into retained earnings, and closing equity equals balance-sheet equity
options.D: Dividends flow into net income, and closing equity equals total assets

questions.rationale: The statement adds net income and OCI, deducts dividends, and adjusts for share issues and buybacks. Its closing totals equal equity on the balance sheet. Equity is a book amount, not cash or market capitalization.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.2 statement of changes in equity

questions.stem: On a statement of financial position, which item is a current liability?

options.A: Long-term debt that is due in five years
options.B: The portion of long-term debt that is due within 12 months
options.C: Deferred tax liabilities that reverse in later years
options.D: Lease liabilities that are due after the next 12 months

questions.rationale: Current items are items that the company expects to settle within 12 months or one operating cycle. So the current portion of long-term debt is current. Deferred tax liabilities and debt due in five years are non-current.

questions.stem: On the statement of comprehensive income, which subtotal shows the result before the effect of debt financing and tax?

options.A: Gross profit (revenue less cost of goods sold)
options.B: EBIT (operating income plus or minus other income)
options.C: Earnings before tax (EBIT less finance costs)
options.D: Net income (earnings before tax less income tax)

questions.rationale: EBIT comes before finance costs and income tax, so it shows the result before debt financing and tax. Earnings before tax already deducts interest. Gross profit shows only the cost of making or buying products.

questions.stem: Which item does a company record in other comprehensive income (OCI), outside profit?

options.A: A gain on the sale of one of its business divisions
options.B: Foreign-currency translation differences on its foreign operations
options.C: Interest that it earns on its cash balances
options.D: Royalties that it earns from licensing its patents

questions.rationale: OCI items, such as foreign-currency translation differences, are recorded outside profit and are mostly unrealized. Interest earned is other income, and royalties are operating revenue. A gain on the sale of a division stays inside profit.

questions.stem: Under the indirect method, how does an increase in accounts receivable affect cash flow from operating activities?

options.A: It is subtracted, because the company has not yet collected the cash
options.B: It is added, because credit sales increase the net income
options.C: It is added back, because it is a non-cash charge like depreciation
options.D: It is excluded, because receivables belong in investing activities

questions.rationale: An increase in receivables uses cash, so the indirect method subtracts it from net income. The company recorded the revenue, but customers have not paid. Depreciation is a non-cash charge, but a receivables increase is a working-capital change.

questions.stem: Which cash flow pattern is the strongest warning sign about a company?

options.A: Negative investing cash flow from capital spending in a growing company
options.B: Negative financing cash flow from dividends and debt repayment in a mature company
options.C: Negative operating cash flow every year, with new borrowing each year to cover it
options.D: Positive financing cash flow in a young company that builds new plant

questions.rationale: A financing inflow that pays for operating losses does not fix the business. It only delays the problem. A young company that raises cash to invest, or a mature company that pays lenders and shareholders, shows a normal pattern.

questions.stem: An auditor's report says that the financial statements present fairly, except for one specific matter. What type of opinion is this?

options.A: A qualified opinion
options.B: An unmodified opinion
options.C: An adverse opinion
options.D: A disclaimer of opinion

questions.rationale: A qualified opinion means that the statements are fair except for a specific matter. An unmodified opinion has no exception. An adverse opinion says that the statements are not fairly presented. A disclaimer means the auditor lacked evidence.

questions.stem: Ravensworth Foods Inc. files an interim financial report. No auditor reviewed it. What does NI 51-102 require?

options.A: A full audit of the report before the company can file it
options.B: A notice with the report that says no auditor reviewed it
options.C: A qualified audit opinion that the company attaches to the report
options.D: A delay of the filing until the annual audit is complete

questions.rationale: If no auditor reviewed an interim report, NI 51-102 s. 4.3(3) requires a notice that says so. Only annual financial statements must be audited (s. 4.1(2)). So a full audit of the interim report is not required.
questions.source_quote: "accompanied by a notice indicating that the interim financial report has not been reviewed by an auditor" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 4.3(3)(a), ~line 890

questions.stem: Ashgrove Tools Ltd. has cash of $60M, marketable securities of $40M, receivables of $140M and inventory of $300M. Its current liabilities are $360M. What is its quick ratio?
questions.rationale: Quick ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = (540 − 300) ÷ 360 = 0.67. The value 1.50 is the current ratio, which includes inventory. The value 0.28 is the cash ratio.

questions.stem: Brackenridge Freight Inc. has EBIT of $96M and interest expense of $24M. In a recession, assume that EBIT falls by 50% and interest does not change. What is the new interest coverage, and what does it show?

options.A: 4.0×; profit covers interest with a wide safety margin
options.B: 0.5×; profit is too low to cover the interest expense
options.C: 2.0×; profit still covers interest, but the safety margin is thin
options.D: 3.0×; profit covers interest with a moderate safety margin

questions.rationale: Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest = (96 × 0.5) ÷ 24 = 2.0×. EBIT still covers interest twice, but a further fall would threaten payment. The value 4.0× is the coverage before the recession.

questions.stem: Over three years, Corvallis Brands Inc. keeps a gross margin near 38%. Its net margin falls from 9% to 6%. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Price cuts on its products to win market share
options.B: Higher overhead, interest or income tax costs
options.C: Higher purchase costs for its raw materials
options.D: A sales shift toward its low-margin products

questions.rationale: Gross margin reflects prices, input costs and product mix. It is stable, so these did not change much. A lower net margin with a stable gross margin points to overhead, interest or tax.

questions.stem: Delmore Home Goods Inc. had inventory turnover of 7.0× and then 6.0× in the last two years. This year, COGS is $960M and year-end inventory is $240M. What does the trend suggest?

options.A: Turnover is 4.0×; inventory sells faster, which helps liquidity
options.B: Turnover is 6.0×; the company uses its inventory as before
options.C: Turnover is 4.0×; weaker demand or obsolete inventory is possible
options.D: Turnover is 0.25×; the company holds too little inventory

questions.rationale: Inventory turnover = COGS ÷ inventory = 960 ÷ 240 = 4.0×. It fell from 7.0× to 6.0× to 4.0×, so inventory sells more slowly. Lower turnover over several periods signals weaker demand or obsolete inventory.

questions.stem: Ellesmere Packaging Ltd. reports operating cash flow of $420M and capex of $310M. It repaid a net $40M of debt and paid dividends of $90M. What is its FCFE, and does it cover the dividend?

options.A: $150M; FCFE covers the dividend with room to spare
options.B: $110M; FCFE covers the dividend with a small margin
options.C: −$20M; the company cannot pay any dividend at all
options.D: $70M; FCFE does not cover the $90M dividend

questions.rationale: FCFE = operating cash flow − capex + net borrowing = 420 − 310 − 40 = $70M. Net debt repayment is negative borrowing, so it reduces FCFE. FCFE of $70M is below the $90M dividend.

questions.stem: Fairhaven Grocers Inc. trades at $27.00. Its EPS is $1.80, and its dividends per share are $0.54. What is its P/E ratio?
questions.rationale: P/E = price ÷ EPS = 27.00 ÷ 1.80 = 15.0×. The value 50.0× divides the price by the dividend, not by EPS. The value 3.3× is the dividend cover, EPS ÷ DPS.

questions.stem: Glenbrook Steel Corp. shares fell from $36 to $18. It pays dividends of $1.26 a share, and its EPS is $0.90. Client Ottilie Marchetti wants to buy for the yield. What is the best assessment?

options.A: Yield is 3.5% and cover is 1.40×, so the dividend is safe
options.B: Yield is 7.0% and cover is 0.71×, so a dividend cut is a real risk
options.C: Yield is 7.0% and cover is 1.40×, so earnings cover the dividend well
options.D: Yield is 5.0% and cover is 0.71×, so the yield is below average

questions.rationale: Dividend yield = 1.26 ÷ 18 = 7.0%. Dividend cover = EPS ÷ DPS = 0.90 ÷ 1.26 = 0.71×, so the dividend exceeds earnings. The high yield comes from the price fall. The value 1.40× inverts the cover formula.

questions.stem: Harwick Software Inc. reported EPS of $2.00, $2.40 and $2.76 over the last three years. Which statement about the trend is correct?

options.A: EPS rises each year, by a larger percentage each year
options.B: EPS rises each year, by the same 20% each year
options.C: EPS rises each year, by the same $0.40 each year
options.D: EPS rises each year, but by a smaller percentage each year

questions.rationale: EPS growth is (2.40 − 2.00) ÷ 2.00 = 20%, then (2.76 − 2.40) ÷ 2.40 = 15%. EPS rises, but the rate of growth slows. The dollar increase also falls, from $0.40 to $0.36.

questions.stem: A securities regulator issued a cease trade order (CTO) against Ironvale Gold Ltd. The CTO is still in effect. Client Leopold Haverty asks his RR to buy the shares over-the-counter. What should the RR tell him?

options.A: The RR can execute the order over-the-counter, because the CTO applies only to exchanges
options.B: The RR can execute the order on the TSX if the client accepts the risk in writing
options.C: No order can be executed on a marketplace or over-the-counter while the CTO is in effect
options.D: The RR can execute the order once the company files a news release on the CTO

questions.rationale: UMIR 9.1(1)(a) bans the execution of any order on a marketplace or over-the-counter while a CTO remains in effect. Client consent does not override the ban. The CTO stays until the regulator revokes it.
questions.source_quote: "an order of a securities regulatory authority to cease trading in the security, derivative, related security or related derivative remains in effect" — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR 9.1(1)(a), ~line 12060

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes who imposes each type of trading stop?

options.A: CIRO issues a CTO, and a securities regulator imposes a regulatory halt
options.B: The exchange issues a CTO, and the company imposes a regulatory halt
options.C: A securities regulator issues a CTO, and CIRO imposes a regulatory halt
options.D: The company issues a CTO, and the exchange imposes a regulatory halt

questions.rationale: A CTO comes from a securities regulator. After a CSA regulator issues a CTO, CIRO, the market regulator, imposes a regulatory halt (NP 11-207 s. 12).
questions.source_quote: "if a CSA regulator issues a cease trade order with respect to an issuer whose securities are traded on a marketplace, IIROC imposes a regulatory halt on trading of those securities on all marketplaces for which IIROC acts as the regulation services provider" — research/sources/csa/np-11-207-failure-to-file-cease-trade-orders.txt NP 11-207 s. 12, ~line 327

questions.stem: In a price-weighted index, which constituent stock has the largest effect on the index level?

options.A: The stock with the highest share price
options.B: The stock with the largest market capitalization
options.C: The stock with the largest public float
options.D: The stock with the most trading volume

questions.rationale: In a price-weighted index, each stock's weight is proportional to its share price, regardless of company size. Market capitalization and float decide weights in a cap-weighted, float-adjusted index such as the S&P/TSX Composite.

questions.stem: Which statement about an equal-weighted index is correct?

options.A: It gives the largest companies the most weight in the index
options.B: It sets each stock's weight in proportion to its share price
options.C: It never needs rebalancing, because its weights stay equal
options.D: It needs regular rebalancing and tilts toward smaller companies

questions.rationale: An equal-weighted index gives every stock the same weight. Prices move apart, so it needs rebalancing to restore equal weights. Compared with a cap-weighted index, it tilts toward smaller companies.

questions.stem: Client Rosalind Achebe has a 70/30 balanced portfolio that returned 7.0% last year. The equity total-return index gained 10.0%, and the bond universe total-return index gained 2.0%. How did the portfolio perform against a blended benchmark?

options.A: It underperformed by 0.6 percentage points
options.B: It outperformed by 1.0 percentage point
options.C: It underperformed by 3.0 percentage points
options.D: It outperformed by 5.0 percentage points

questions.rationale: Blended benchmark = 0.70 × 10.0% + 0.30 × 2.0% = 7.6%. Relative return = 7.0% − 7.6% = −0.6 points. A comparison with the equity index alone (−3.0 points) ignores the 30% bond weight.

questions.stem: RR Casimir Lindqvist manages a broad Canadian equity portfolio with a total return of 6.5%. The S&P/TSX Composite had a price return of 4.0% and a total return of 7.0%. What is the correct relative return?

options.A: +2.5 points, against the price-return index
options.B: −0.5 points, against the total-return index
options.C: +0.5 points, against the total-return index
options.D: −2.5 points, against the price-return index

questions.rationale: The portfolio's 6.5% includes dividends, so compare it with the total-return index: 6.5% − 7.0% = −0.5 points. A price-return benchmark omits dividends and makes the portfolio look 2.5 points better.

questions.stem: Analyst Wendeline Ostrowski says that Kingsmere Rail's shares are below their 200-day moving average and near a support level. She does not use financial statements. Which assumption underlies her method?

options.A: Prices move toward intrinsic value, which depends on forecast cash flows
options.B: The peer group is fairly priced, so a relative P/E shows value
options.C: Markets are efficient, so no method can earn abnormal returns
options.D: Prices adjust gradually to information, so trends persist and patterns repeat

questions.rationale: Moving averages and support levels are technical analysis tools. Technical analysis assumes that prices adjust gradually, so they move in trends and patterns repeat. The intrinsic-value assumption belongs to fundamental analysis.

questions.stem: A dealer's research report sets a $75 price target on Lakehurst Pipelines Inc., which trades at $58. Client Thaddeus Nkemelu asks whether the target is reliable. What should his RR do?

options.A: Accept the target, because a dealer's research report is a public filing
options.B: Find the disclosed valuation method, then test the key assumptions behind it
options.C: Compare the target with the stock's 200-day moving average only
options.D: Tell the client that targets need no stated method, so none can be tested

questions.rationale: If a dealer sets a price target in a research report, IDPC 3616(1) requires the report to disclose the valuation method. The RR can then test assumptions such as growth or the discount rate. Research is opinion, not a filing.
questions.source_quote: "If a Dealer Member sets a price target in a research report, the Dealer Member must disclose, in that research report, the valuation method used." — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3616(1), ~line 7459

questions.stem: Why do analysts often value a manufacturing company on its average earnings over a full cycle?

options.A: High fixed costs make profits swing widely, so one year's P/E can mislead
options.B: Its assets are mainly financial, so price-to-book is a better measure
options.C: Regulation fixes its revenue, so one year's earnings show the full picture
options.D: It pays no dividends, so the P/E ratio cannot be calculated for it

questions.rationale: Manufacturers have high fixed costs, so a small change in sales gives a large change in profit. One year's P/E can mislead at the top of the cycle. Price-to-book suits banks, whose assets are mainly financial.

questions.stem: A quarterly report shows that productivity rose faster than economists expected, while wages grew steadily. What is the most likely market effect?

options.A: Margins improve and inflation pressure eases, giving the central bank room to hold rates
options.B: Inflation pressure rises, so the central bank must raise rates sooner
options.C: Unit labour costs rise, so company margins and earnings fall
options.D: Bond prices fall, because higher output always pushes yields up

questions.rationale: Productivity is output per hour of work. If it rises faster than wages, unit labour costs fall, so margins improve without higher prices. The economy can grow with less inflation, so the central bank has room to hold rates.

questions.stem: Client Benedikt Szabo plans to hold equities for 25 years. Which statement about his long time horizon is correct?

options.A: It removes the risk of a loss in any single year of the period
options.B: It narrows the range of final dollar wealth that he can expect
options.C: It makes his expected equity return equal to the return on bonds
options.D: It narrows the spread of average annual returns, but not the risk of a loss in any year

questions.rationale: Over long horizons, the spread of average annual returns narrows. But the range of final dollar wealth does not narrow, and a loss can still occur in any single year. Equities keep the highest expected return.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.14 volatility and exam trap

questions.stem: Which event at Marlowe Freightways Inc. best fits the NI 51-102 meaning of a material change?

options.A: An analyst at another dealer lowers its rating on Marlowe shares
options.B: Marlowe shares rise 8% on the same day as a broad market rally
options.C: A competitor of Marlowe reports higher quarterly earnings
options.D: The Marlowe board decides to sell the company's main operating division

questions.rationale: A material change is a change in the company's business, operations or capital that can significantly affect its share price. A board decision to make such a change also counts. A rating change by an outside analyst is not a change in Marlowe's business.
questions.source_quote: "a decision to implement a change referred to in paragraph (a) made by the board of directors" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 1.1 'material change' (b), ~line 340

questions.stem: Pendrell Oil Corp. is in talks to buy a rival. In its reasonable opinion, disclosure now would be unduly detrimental to its interests. What does NI 51-102 let Pendrell do?

options.A: File the material change report marked confidential, with written reasons for non-disclosure
options.B: Wait until the deal closes, and file nothing with the regulator until then
options.C: Tell its five largest shareholders about the talks, but issue no news release
options.D: Issue the news release now, but leave out the name of the rival company

questions.rationale: Under NI 51-102 s. 7.1(2), the company can skip the news release. But it must immediately file the report marked confidential, with written reasons. Filing nothing is not allowed, and telling a few shareholders is selective disclosure.
questions.source_quote: "immediately files the report required under paragraph (1)(b) marked so as to indicate that it is confidential, together with written reasons for non-disclosure" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 7.1(2), ~line 2516

questions.stem: Ashcombe Lithium Ltd. filed a confidential material change report. The change is still not public. What must Ashcombe do while the report stays confidential?

options.A: File a new material change report each month until the board approves the change
options.B: Tell the regulator in writing every 10 days if it believes the report should stay confidential
options.C: Ask the exchange to halt trading in its shares until it discloses the change
options.D: Send a private summary of the change to its auditor every 30 days

questions.rationale: NI 51-102 s. 7.1(5) requires written advice to the regulator within 10 days of the filing and every 10 days after that. The rule does not require monthly reports or notices to the auditor.
questions.source_quote: "the reporting issuer must advise the regulator or securities regulatory authority in writing if it believes the report should continue to remain confidential, within 10 days of the date of filing of the initial report and every 10 days thereafter" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 7.1(5), ~line 2522

questions.stem: Senior management of Grantley Mills Inc. decides to close its largest plant. They expect the board to confirm the decision next week. Which fact stops Grantley from keeping the change confidential?

options.A: The board has not yet met to confirm the decision
options.B: Management believes that the board will probably confirm the decision
options.C: Management has reason to believe that two employees bought shares because they knew of the decision
options.D: The plant closure would reasonably be expected to affect the share price

questions.rationale: The senior-management exception applies only if management has no reason to believe that people traded with knowledge of the change. The pending board vote and the expected board approval are conditions of the exception, not obstacles to it.
questions.source_quote: "senior management of the reporting issuer has no reason to believe that persons with knowledge of" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 7.1(2)(b), ~line 2503

questions.stem: Ravensholt Foods Inc. learns that it will lose its largest customer. Its CEO wants to delay the news until the company can also announce a new contract. Which principle does this plan break?

options.A: Unfavourable news must be disclosed just as promptly and completely as favourable news
options.B: A company can delay bad news if the board expects good news within one quarter
options.C: A company discloses material news only in its next interim financial report
options.D: Bad news needs disclosure only when the share price has already started to fall

questions.rationale: NP 51-201 s. 2.1(2) says that unfavourable news must be disclosed just as promptly and completely as favourable news. A company cannot hold bad news to pair it with good news. The other options describe delays that the policy does not allow.
questions.source_quote: "Unfavourable news must be disclosed just as promptly and completely as favourable news." — research/sources/csa/np-51-201-disclosure-standards.txt NP 51-201 s. 2.1(2), ~line 127

questions.stem: Before any news release, the CFO of Dunmore Textiles Ltd. tells three institutional analysts that quarterly earnings will be lower than expected. What is the main concern?

options.A: Selective disclosure of material nonpublic information can create opportunities for insider trading
options.B: The CFO must first get the auditor's approval of the quarterly earnings
options.C: The analysts must publish the information in a research report within 10 days
options.D: The CFO gave a forecast that the AIF must label as an opinion

questions.rationale: The CFO gave material nonpublic information to a few people, not to the public. NP 51-201 s. 1.1 says that selective disclosure can create opportunities for insider trading. The analysts have no duty to publish it.
questions.source_quote: "Selective disclosure can create opportunities for insider trading" — research/sources/csa/np-51-201-disclosure-standards.txt NP 51-201 s. 1.1(1), ~line 83

questions.stem: Client Severin Okafor wants management's own explanation of the reasons for Ellery Tools Inc.'s weak results last quarter. Which filed document should his RR use?

options.A: The Annual Information Form (AIF) from last year
options.B: The auditor's report on last year's annual financial statements
options.C: The MD&A filed with the interim financial report for the quarter
options.D: The information circular for the next shareholder meeting

questions.rationale: NI 51-102 s. 5.1(1) requires MD&A with the annual statements and each interim report. It gives management's discussion of results. The AIF is an annual overview, and the auditor's report covers only the annual statements.
questions.source_quote: "A reporting issuer must file MD&A relating to its annual financial statements and each interim financial report required under Part 4." — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 5.1(1), ~line 2186

questions.stem: Client Liesl Varga sees a clean audit opinion on the statements of Thornwick Media. She says that this proves the MD&A's growth forecast is reliable. How should her RR respond?

options.A: The forecast is reliable, because the auditor's opinion covers every document in the annual filing
options.B: The forecast is reliable, because the MD&A must use the same numbers as the audited statements
options.C: The forecast is unreliable, because a clean opinion means that the auditor found errors in the MD&A
options.D: The auditor's opinion covers the financial statements, not management's commentary in the MD&A

questions.rationale: The MD&A is a management document. The auditor's opinion covers the financial statements only. So a clean opinion does not test management's forecast. A clean opinion also does not mean that the auditor found errors.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.1 exam trap (MD&A and AIF are management documents; audit covers the statements)

questions.stem: Client Anselm Kowal asks his RR how a foreign dividend will be taxed in his account. The RR is not sure of the tax rules. What should the RR do?

options.A: Give his best estimate now, and correct it later if a tax adviser disagrees
options.B: Consult a tax expert before he answers, record the advice and name its source to Anselm
options.C: Tell Anselm that tax questions are outside the RR's role, and close the request
options.D: Ask the dealer's investment banking staff, because they deal with foreign issuers

questions.rationale: If a question goes beyond the RR's knowledge, he asks an expert before he answers, records the advice and tells the client the source. A guess can lead to a decision on wrong information. Information barriers limit contacts with investment banking staff.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.1 collaboration with internal and external experts

questions.stem: A dealer's newsletter to all clients praises the 9% yield on Halloway Energy Trust units. It does not mention that the trust cut its payout twice in two years. Which IDPC 3602(1) defect does it have?

options.A: It uses a yield figure that the dealer did not calculate
options.B: It names an issuer that the dealer does not cover with research
options.C: It is correspondence that went to more than one client
options.D: It fails to fairly present the potential risks to the client

questions.rationale: IDPC 3602(1)(v) prohibits sales literature that fails to fairly present the potential risks. The newsletter hides the payout cuts that put the yield at risk. A newsletter to all clients is sales literature, not correspondence to a single client.
questions.source_quote: "fails to fairly present the potential risks to the client" — research/sources/ciro/idpc-rules-2026-08-11.txt IDPC 3602(1)(v), ~line 7289

questions.stem: Fernleigh Brewing Ltd. has a market capitalization four times its book equity. Which reason best explains the gap?

options.A: Many assets stay at historical cost less depreciation, and internal brands are often not recorded
options.B: Accountants record all assets at current market value, and investors then add a premium
options.C: Book equity includes all liabilities, so it is always much smaller than the share price total
options.D: Retained earnings are paid out as dividends, so they do not appear in book equity

questions.rationale: Plant and equipment often stay at historical cost less depreciation. The company often does not record internally built intangibles, such as a brand. So book value is not market value. Assets are not all recorded at market value.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.2 book value is not market value

questions.stem: Which statement about retained earnings on a company's balance sheet is correct?

options.A: It is a cash reserve that the company keeps in the bank to pay future dividends
options.B: It is a current asset that the company can use to pay its suppliers
options.C: It is the total of past profits that the company kept, and it is part of equity, not cash
options.D: It is the amount of profit that the company must pay as dividends next year

questions.rationale: Retained earnings is the total of past profits that the company did not pay as dividends. It is a source of financing inside equity, not an amount of cash. The company has already used that money to buy assets.

questions.stem: On a statement of financial position, which item is part of shareholders' equity?

options.A: Deferred tax liabilities
options.B: Goodwill from a past acquisition
options.C: Prepaid expenses
options.D: Accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI)

questions.rationale: Equity includes share capital, contributed surplus, retained earnings and AOCI. Deferred tax liabilities are non-current liabilities. Goodwill is a non-current asset, and prepaid expenses are a current asset.

questions.stem: Which items does the statement of changes in equity deduct when it moves from opening equity to closing equity?

options.A: Depreciation and interest expense
options.B: Dividends and share buybacks
options.C: Capital expenditures and acquisitions
options.D: Repayments of long-term debt

questions.rationale: The statement adds net income, OCI and share issues, and it deducts dividends and share buybacks. Depreciation and interest reduce net income on the income statement. Capex and debt repayments are cash flows that do not change equity.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.2 statement of changes in equity

questions.stem: Under NI 51-102, which set of statements must a reporting issuer's annual financial statements include?

options.A: Comprehensive income, changes in equity, cash flows, financial position and notes
options.B: Comprehensive income, financial position, cash flows and the MD&A
options.C: Financial position, comprehensive income and the Annual Information Form
options.D: Financial position, cash flows and notes, without a statement of changes in equity

questions.rationale: NI 51-102 s. 4.1(1) lists a statement of comprehensive income, a statement of changes in equity and a statement of cash flows. It also lists a statement of financial position and notes. The MD&A and AIF are separate filings.
questions.source_quote: "a reporting issuer must file annual financial statements that include (a) a statement of comprehensive income, a statement of changes in equity, and a statement of cash flows" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 4.1(1)(a), ~line 782

questions.stem: On the statement of comprehensive income, which subtotal best shows how efficiently a company makes or buys the products that it sells?

options.A: Net income
options.B: Earnings before tax
options.C: Gross profit
options.D: Total comprehensive income

questions.rationale: Gross profit is revenue minus cost of goods sold, so it shows the efficiency of making or buying products. Net income and earnings before tax also include overhead, interest and other costs.

questions.stem: During the year, Harcastle Retail Inc. sold a major line of business. How does it show that line's result on the statement of comprehensive income?

options.A: As part of operating revenue, together with the continuing business
options.B: On a separate line, after profit from continuing operations
options.C: In other comprehensive income, outside profit
options.D: Only in the statement of cash flows, not in profit

questions.rationale: A company shows the result of a major line of business that it sold or closed on a separate line, after profit from continuing operations. OCI holds items such as currency translation, not discontinued operations.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.3 sources of income (discontinued operations)

questions.stem: Over the last year, gains on asset sales gave Corrigan Chemicals Ltd. 30% of its pre-tax profit. An analyst forecasts next year's earnings. What is the best approach?

options.A: Use this year's net income as the base, because all income has equal quality
options.B: Add the asset-sale gains to operating revenue, because they increase profit
options.C: Ignore operating income, because one-time gains drive the share value
options.D: Separate the gains from operating revenue, because recurring operating income is a better guide

questions.rationale: Other income, such as gains on asset sales, can be large in one year and absent in the next. Recurring operating income is usually a better guide to future earnings. So analysts separate the gains when they forecast.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.3 sources of income (recurring vs other income)

questions.stem: Which amount is the basis for a company's earnings per share (EPS)?

options.A: Profit attributable to common shareholders
options.B: Total comprehensive income
options.C: Operating income before other income
options.D: Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT)

questions.rationale: EPS uses profit attributable to common shareholders. It does not use total comprehensive income, which also includes OCI items that the company records outside profit. EBIT and operating income come before interest and tax.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.3 exam trap (EPS uses profit, not total comprehensive income)

questions.stem: Lindqvale Paper Corp. shows profit or loss in a separate income statement. Under NI 51-102, where must that statement appear?

options.A: Immediately after the statement of cash flows
options.B: In the notes, after the accounting policies
options.C: Immediately before the statement of comprehensive income
options.D: Inside the MD&A, with management's discussion

questions.rationale: NI 51-102 s. 4.1(3) says that the separate income statement must be displayed immediately before the statement of comprehensive income. The other placements do not follow the rule.
questions.source_quote: "the separate income statement must be displayed immediately before the statement of comprehensive income filed under subsection (1)" — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 4.1(3), ~line 825

questions.stem: Under the indirect method, why does a company add back depreciation to net income to get operating cash flow?

options.A: Depreciation is a cash payment that the company makes in the next year
options.B: Depreciation is a financing cost, so it belongs in the financing section
options.C: Depreciation increases the company's cash when the assets get older
options.D: Depreciation reduced net income but did not use any cash in the period

questions.rationale: The indirect method starts with net income and adds back non-cash charges, such as depreciation and amortization. Depreciation reduces profit, but no cash leaves the company for it in the period. It is not a financing cost.

questions.stem: Over the year, unpaid supplier bills at Westbury Cabinets Inc. rose by $15M. Where and how does this change appear in the statement of cash flows?

options.A: In the operating section, as an addition to net income
options.B: In the financing section, as new borrowing
options.C: In the operating section, as a deduction from net income
options.D: In the investing section, as a cash inflow

questions.rationale: Higher accounts payable keep cash in the company, so the indirect method adds the increase in the operating section. Trade payables are a working-capital item, not interest-bearing borrowing in the financing section.

questions.stem: Which transaction does a company report in the financing section of its statement of cash flows?

options.A: Buying marketable securities with excess cash
options.B: Paying suppliers for raw materials
options.C: Selling a used delivery truck
options.D: Buying back its own common shares

questions.rationale: Financing activities are cash flows with lenders and shareholders, such as share buybacks, dividends and debt. Buying securities and selling equipment are investing activities. Payments to suppliers are operating activities.

questions.stem: Kilbride Utilities Inc. is a mature company. It has large positive operating cash flow, and its financing cash flow is negative from dividends and debt repayment. What does this pattern usually show?

options.A: A warning sign, because the company pays out more cash than it raises
options.B: A healthy pattern, because operating cash flow is large enough to pay lenders and shareholders
options.C: A sign of fast growth, because the company invests all of its cash in new assets
options.D: A liquidity problem, because negative financing cash flow reduces profit

questions.rationale: In a mature company, a financing outflow is usually healthy. It means that operating cash flow is large enough to repay debt and pay dividends. A negative financing number alone is not a warning sign, and it does not reduce profit.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.4 financing activities by company stage

questions.stem: Over three years, Norland Robotics Ltd., a young company, raised new equity each year. It spent the cash on new plants, and its operating cash flow is starting to grow. How should an analyst view the financing inflows?

options.A: As a warning sign, because any financing inflow means that the business is weak
options.B: As a problem, because a company should pay for new plants only from profit
options.C: As normal, because the cash goes into investing activities that can produce future operating cash flow
options.D: As a sign that the company has more cash than it needs for its operations

questions.rationale: A young company that grows fast often shows financing inflows. This is normal if the cash goes into investing activities that can produce future operating cash flow. An inflow becomes a warning sign when it pays for operating losses year after year.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.4 financing activities by company stage

questions.stem: Strathmore Packaging Corp. reports negative cash flow from investing activities each year. What does this usually mean?

options.A: The company reinvests in long-term assets to grow or to replace worn-out assets
options.B: The company loses money on its core business and borrows to cover the losses
options.C: The company pays more in dividends and buybacks than it raises from lenders
options.D: The company collects cash from customers more slowly than it pays suppliers

questions.rationale: The investing section shows spending on long-term assets and investments. A negative number usually means that the company reinvests to grow or to replace worn-out assets. Dividends and buybacks are financing items, and collections are operating items.

questions.stem: An auditor concludes that a company's financial statements are not fairly presented. Which type of opinion does the auditor give?

options.A: An unmodified opinion
options.B: A qualified opinion
options.C: An adverse opinion
options.D: A disclaimer of opinion

questions.rationale: An adverse opinion says that the statements are not fairly presented. A qualified opinion says that they are fair except for a specific matter. A disclaimer means that the auditor could not obtain enough evidence to give an opinion.

questions.stem: The auditor of Tavistock Diagnostics Ltd. gives an unmodified opinion. The report also has a "Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern" section. What does this show?

options.A: The statements contain a material error that management refused to correct
options.B: The statements are fairly presented, but the company's ability to continue in business is in doubt
options.C: The auditor could not get enough evidence, so the opinion is not reliable
options.D: The company is safe, because an unmodified opinion removes any going-concern doubt

questions.rationale: An unmodified opinion means only that the statements are fairly presented. A separate going-concern section is a warning sign that the company's ability to continue in business is in doubt. It does not mean an error or a lack of evidence.

questions.stem: An analyst studies Brookhaven Cement Inc. Which information will she most likely find in the notes, and not as a number on the balance sheet?

options.A: The total value of inventory at year-end
options.B: A pending lawsuit that the company discloses as a contingency
options.C: The balance of accounts receivable at year-end
options.D: The amount of share capital at year-end

questions.rationale: The notes disclose contingencies, such as lawsuits, plus debt covenants and other commitments. Many such risks never appear as a balance-sheet number. Inventory, receivables and share capital are balance-sheet amounts.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.5 notes to the financial statements

questions.stem: Under NI 51-102, which statement about audits of a reporting issuer's financial statements is correct?

options.A: Annual financial statements must be audited, but auditors usually do not audit interim reports
options.B: Annual and interim financial statements must both have a full audit
options.C: Only the MD&A and the AIF must be audited each year
options.D: Audits are optional if the company files its statements on time

questions.rationale: NI 51-102 s. 4.1(2) says that annual financial statements must be audited. Auditors usually do not audit interim reports. If no auditor reviewed an interim report, it carries a notice that says so.
questions.source_quote: "Annual financial statements filed under subsection (1) must be audited." — research/sources/csa/ni-51-102-continuous-disclosure-obligations.txt NI 51-102 s. 4.1(2), ~line 822

questions.stem: Ridgeway Cobalt Corp. does not file its annual audited financial statements by the deadline. How do the CSA regulators generally respond to this specified default?

options.A: They delist the company from all exchanges at the end of the month
options.B: They fine each director, but trading in the shares continues as normal
options.C: They issue a failure-to-file CTO, or a management CTO if the company applies and can comply
options.D: They wait for the next annual filing and take no action until then

questions.rationale: NP 11-207 s. 6 says that the CSA regulators generally respond in one of two ways. They issue a failure-to-file CTO, or a management CTO if the company applies under NP 12-203 and shows that it can comply.
questions.source_quote: "The CSA regulators will then generally respond to a specified default in one of two ways:" — research/sources/csa/np-11-207-failure-to-file-cease-trade-orders.txt NP 11-207 s. 6, ~line 190

questions.stem: Client Jorund Hallam says that a clean audit opinion guarantees that a company's statements contain no fraud. Which response is correct?

options.A: He is right, because the auditor checks every transaction in the year
options.B: He is right, because the regulator also reviews each audit before filing
options.C: He is wrong, because an audit tests only the MD&A, not the statements
options.D: He is wrong, because an audit gives reasonable assurance, not a guarantee against fraud or error

questions.rationale: An audit gives reasonable assurance that the statements are fairly presented. It is not a guarantee against fraud or error. The audit covers the financial statements, not the MD&A.

questions.stem: Ivybridge Instruments Ltd. has cash of $45M, marketable securities of $35M, receivables of $90M and inventory of $150M. Its current liabilities are $200M. What is its cash ratio?
questions.rationale: Cash ratio = (cash + marketable securities) ÷ current liabilities = 80 ÷ 200 = 0.40. The value 0.85 is the quick ratio, which also counts receivables. The value 1.60 is the current ratio.

questions.stem: Pellworth Ltd. and Quinlan Corp. each have current assets of $500M and current liabilities of $250M. Pellworth holds $100M of inventory, and Quinlan holds $350M. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Both are equally liquid, because both have a current ratio of 2.0
options.B: Pellworth is more liquid; its quick ratio is 1.6, against 0.6 for Quinlan
options.C: Quinlan is more liquid, because inventory is the most liquid current asset
options.D: Quinlan is more liquid; its quick ratio is 1.4, against 0.4 for Pellworth

questions.rationale: Quick ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities. Pellworth: 400 ÷ 250 = 1.6. Quinlan: 150 ÷ 250 = 0.6. Equal current ratios hide the difference, because inventory can be slow to sell.

questions.stem: Kingsbarrow Transit Inc. has a bank loan of $40M, long-term debt of $260M, accounts payable of $90M and equity of $600M. Use interest-bearing debt. What is its debt-to-equity ratio?
questions.rationale: Debt-to-equity = interest-bearing debt ÷ equity = (40 + 260) ÷ 600 = 0.50. The value 0.65 wrongly adds accounts payable, which is not interest-bearing. The value 0.43 leaves out the bank loan.

questions.stem: Oakhurst Ceramics Ltd. has revenue of $800M, COGS of $520M, operating expenses of $160M and interest expense of $20M. Its tax rate is 25%. What is its pre-tax margin?
questions.rationale: EBIT = 800 − 520 − 160 = 120. EBT = 120 − 20 = 100. Pre-tax margin = EBT ÷ revenue = 100 ÷ 800 = 12.5%. The value 15.0% uses EBIT, before interest. The value 9.4% is the net margin, after tax.

questions.stem: Sandgate Logistics Inc. has net income of $90M, EBIT of $140M, total assets of $1,200M and equity of $600M. What is its return on assets?
questions.rationale: Return on assets = net income ÷ total assets = 90 ÷ 1,200 = 7.5%. The value 15.0% divides net income by equity, not by assets. The value 11.7% uses EBIT, not net income.

questions.stem: Tremont Aggregates Corp. has EBIT of $200M, interest expense of $30M and a tax rate of 25%. Its total debt is $400M, and its equity is $800M. What is its return on invested capital (ROIC)?
questions.rationale: ROIC = EBIT × (1 − t) ÷ (debt + equity) = 200 × 0.75 ÷ 1,200 = 12.5%. The value 16.7% ignores tax. The value 10.6% uses net income, which deducts interest, so it understates the return to all capital.

questions.stem: Last year, Upton Dairy Ltd. had receivables turnover of 9.0×. This year, revenue is $1,800M, COGS is $1,200M and year-end receivables are $300M. What does the change show?

options.A: Turnover is 6.0×; customers pay more slowly than last year
options.B: Turnover is 6.0×; customers pay faster than last year
options.C: Turnover is 4.0×; customers pay more slowly than last year
options.D: Turnover is 0.17×; the company cannot collect from its customers

questions.rationale: Receivables turnover = revenue ÷ receivables = 1,800 ÷ 300 = 6.0×. A fall from 9.0× means slower collection. The value 4.0× wrongly uses COGS, which the convention keeps for inventory and payables turnover.

questions.stem: Vellacombe Hardware Inc. has receivables turnover of 6× and payables turnover of 12×. What does this comparison suggest?

options.A: It collects from customers faster than it pays suppliers, which helps liquidity
options.B: It turns over its inventory twice as fast as its receivables
options.C: It collects from customers more slowly than it pays suppliers, which strains liquidity
options.D: It uses its fixed assets twice as efficiently as its peers

questions.rationale: A receivables turnover of 6× is slower than a payables turnover of 12×. So cash leaves for suppliers faster than it comes in from customers, which strains liquidity. The comparison says nothing about inventory or fixed assets.
questions.qa_note: concept/calc: guide 4.6 efficiency ratios (collect 16.7x vs pay 8.0x helps liquidity; inverse here)

questions.stem: Winsford Printing Ltd. has revenue of $2,400M, current assets of $700M and current liabilities of $400M. What is its working capital turnover?
questions.rationale: Working capital turnover = revenue ÷ (current assets − current liabilities) = 2,400 ÷ 300 = 8.0×. The value 3.4× divides by current assets only. The value 6.0× divides by current liabilities only.

questions.stem: Yarrowby Foods Inc. has net income of $66M and pays preferred dividends of $6M. It has a weighted average of 30M common shares, and 32M at year-end. What is its EPS?
questions.rationale: EPS = (net income − preferred dividends) ÷ weighted average common shares = 60 ÷ 30 = $2.00. The value $2.20 does not deduct preferred dividends. The value $1.88 uses year-end shares, not the weighted average.

questions.stem: Abbotsford Glassworks Ltd. has revenue of $3,000M and net PP&E of $1,200M. Its peers average a fixed asset turnover of 4.0×. What does the comparison suggest?

options.A: Its turnover is 2.5×; it produces less revenue per dollar of plant than its peers
options.B: Its turnover is 2.5×; it produces more revenue per dollar of plant than its peers
options.C: Its turnover is 0.4×; it uses only a small part of its plant
options.D: Its turnover is 4.0×; it uses its plant as efficiently as its peers

questions.rationale: Fixed asset turnover = revenue ÷ net PP&E = 3,000 ÷ 1,200 = 2.5×. This is below the peer average of 4.0×, so it produces less revenue from each dollar of plant. A higher turnover usually means better use of assets.

questions.stem: Bellhaven Textiles Corp. earns net income of $160M and pays common dividends of $40M. It has no preferred shares. What is its retention rate, and what does it show?

options.A: 25%; it keeps a small part of its profit to reinvest in the business
options.B: 75%; it pays most of its profit to shareholders as dividends
options.C: 33%; it keeps one-third of its profit to reinvest in the business
options.D: 75%; it keeps most of its profit to reinvest in the business

questions.rationale: Payout = dividends ÷ net income = 40 ÷ 160 = 25%. Retention rate = 1 − payout = 75%, so the company keeps most of its profit. The value 25% is the payout ratio, not the retention rate.

questions.stem: Carbury Insurance Ltd. has EPS of $3.60 and pays dividends of $1.20 a share. Its shares trade at $48.00. What is its dividend cover, and what does it show?

options.A: 0.33×; the dividend is three times earnings, so a cut is likely
options.B: 3.0×; earnings are three times the dividend, so the dividend looks safe
options.C: 2.5×; earnings cover the dividend with a moderate margin
options.D: 33%; earnings cover only one-third of the dividend

questions.rationale: Dividend cover = EPS ÷ DPS = 3.60 ÷ 1.20 = 3.0×. Earnings pay for the dividend three times, so the payout of about 33% looks safe. The value 0.33× inverts the formula. The value 2.5 is the yield in percent.
questions.qa_note: calc: 3.60/1.20 = 3.0; distractors 1.20/3.60 = 0.33 (inverted), 1.20/48 = 2.5% (yield), payout 33% misread as cover

questions.stem: Denholm Rail Corp. has total equity of $900M, which includes $100M of preferred shares. It has 40M common shares, which trade at $35.00. What is its equity per common share?

options.A: $22.50; the market price is above book value
options.B: $25.00; the market price is above book value
options.C: $20.00; the market price is below book value
options.D: $20.00; the market price is above book value

questions.rationale: Equity per common share = (total equity − preferred equity) ÷ common shares = 800 ÷ 40 = $20.00. The $35.00 price is above it. The value $22.50 wrongly keeps the preferred equity in the common equity.

questions.stem: Last year, Elmstead Chemicals Inc. traded at $27 with EPS of $1.50. This year the price is still $27, but EPS is $0.60. Which statement best explains the change in its P/E?

options.A: The P/E fell from 18× to 4×, so the shares now look cheap
options.B: The P/E rose from 18× to 45×, so investors clearly expect much faster growth
options.C: The P/E rose from 18× to 45×, mainly because earnings fell, not because of growth hopes
options.D: The P/E did not change, because the share price stayed at $27

questions.rationale: P/E = price ÷ EPS: 27 ÷ 1.50 = 18× and 27 ÷ 0.60 = 45×. The price did not move, so the higher P/E comes from lower earnings. A high P/E can reflect temporarily low earnings, not only expected growth.
questions.qa_note: calc: 27/1.5 = 18, 27/0.6 = 45; concept guide 4.7 (high P/E may reflect temporarily low earnings)

questions.stem: Which statement about a company's diluted EPS is correct?

options.A: It counts only the shares outstanding at year-end, so it is higher than basic EPS
options.B: It also counts shares that options and convertible securities could add, so it is equal to or lower than basic EPS
options.C: It uses total comprehensive income, so it is usually higher than basic EPS
options.D: It excludes preferred dividends, so it is always lower than basic EPS

questions.rationale: Diluted EPS also counts the shares that options and convertible securities could add. More shares share the same earnings, so diluted EPS is equal to or lower than basic EPS. Neither EPS measure uses total comprehensive income.

questions.stem: Over four years, Fallowfield Marine Ltd.'s debt-to-equity rose from 0.3 to 0.9. Its interest coverage fell from 12× to 4×. What does this trend show?

options.A: Lower risk, because more debt lets the company grow faster
options.B: Better operations, because the company uses its assets more efficiently
options.C: No change in risk, because the coverage is still above 1×
options.D: Higher financial risk, because the company depends more on debt and covers interest less

questions.rationale: Trend analysis compares a company with itself over several periods. Higher debt-to-equity with lower interest coverage points to more risk. Coverage above 1× still covers interest, but the safety margin is much thinner than before.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.7 trend analysis (higher D/E with lower coverage = more risk)

questions.stem: An analyst sees that a utility has debt-to-equity of 1.5, and a software company has 0.2. She concludes that the utility carries too much debt. What is the main flaw in her method?

options.A: Normal debt levels differ widely by sector, so she should compare the utility with utility peers
options.B: Debt-to-equity is not a risk ratio, so she should use the current ratio instead
options.C: She should compare the two companies' P/E ratios before she looks at their debt
options.D: A utility always has less risk than a software company, whatever its debt

questions.rationale: External comparisons use peers in the same sector, because normal ratio levels differ widely. A utility's normal leverage would alarm you in a software company. Debt-to-equity is a risk ratio, and sector alone does not make a company safe.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.7 external comparisons (utility vs software leverage)

questions.stem: An analyst compares Glenarm Steel Corp.'s ratios with a peer's ratios. Which comparison follows good practice for external comparisons?

options.A: Glenarm's ratios for this year against the peer's ratios from two years ago
options.B: Glenarm's ratios against a peer in the same sector, for the same fiscal period and accounting basis
options.C: Glenarm's ratios against a bank's ratios, because banks publish more data
options.D: Glenarm's ratios under one accounting basis against the peer's under a different basis

questions.rationale: External comparisons must compare like with like: a similar business mix, the same fiscal period and the same accounting basis. Different years, sectors or accounting bases make the gaps between ratios misleading.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.7 external comparisons (like with like)

questions.stem: Stock data for Corbett Mills Inc. shows its market capitalization. How do exchanges and data vendors calculate this figure?

options.A: Daily trading volume multiplied by the last share price
options.B: Share price multiplied by the common shares outstanding
options.C: Total assets minus total liabilities on the balance sheet
options.D: Share price multiplied by the shares that insiders hold

questions.rationale: Market capitalization equals the share price times the common shares outstanding, and it measures company size. Price times daily volume gives the dollar value traded. Total assets minus total liabilities is book equity, not a market value.

questions.stem: Shares of Tamsin Robotics Inc. rise 5% in one day. The volume is four times the stock's daily average. What does the high volume tell an analyst?

options.A: The company issued new shares to the public that day
options.B: The bid-ask spread on the stock became wider that day
options.C: The stock now trades above its intrinsic value
options.D: Many investors took part, so the price move is more significant

questions.rationale: Volume counts the shares traded, and it shows how significant a price move is. A move on heavy volume has wide participation. Volume alone says nothing about intrinsic value, which needs fundamental analysis.

questions.stem: A data vendor quotes a Government of Canada bond at a price of 98.50. What does this price mean?

options.A: The bond trades at $98.50 for each $100 of face value
options.B: The bond trades at $98.50 for each $1,000 of face value
options.C: The bond pays a coupon equal to 98.50% of its face value
options.D: The bond has a yield to maturity of 9.85% a year

questions.rationale: Bond prices are quoted per $100 of face value. So 98.50 means $98.50 per $100, a small discount to face value. The quote is not a coupon rate, and the yield to maturity is a separate data item.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.8 fixed-income data (price per $100 of face value)

questions.stem: Halloway Minerals Ltd., an Ontario reporting issuer, does not file a record that the Securities Act requires. What can the Ontario Securities Commission do?

options.A: Only ask CIRO to fine the company's directors
options.B: Issue a cease trade order, but only after a full hearing
options.C: Order that trading stop, without first giving the company a hearing
options.D: Only issue a public warning, because a missed filing is not a trading matter

questions.rationale: Ontario Securities Act s. 127(4.1) covers a company that fails to file a required record. The Commission can then order that trading cease without a hearing. A hearing is not a precondition for this failure-to-file order.
questions.source_quote: "without giving the person or company that is subject to the order an opportunity to be heard if the person or company fails to file a record required to be filed under this Act" — research/sources/gov/ontario-securities-act-extracts.txt Ontario Securities Act s. 127(4.1), ~line 653

questions.stem: The Ontario Securities Commission issued a failure-to-file CTO against Quenby Textiles Inc. 40 days ago. Quenby now files the missing annual statements. What must the Commission do?

options.A: Revoke the order as soon as practicable after the filing
options.B: Keep the order in effect for at least 90 days in total
options.C: Require more records from Quenby before it revokes the order
options.D: Hold a hearing before it decides to revoke the order

questions.rationale: Ontario Securities Act s. 127(4.3) requires the Commission to revoke the order as soon as practicable after the record is filed. It can require more records first only if the order is more than 90 days old. This order is 40 days old.
questions.source_quote: "Subject to subsection (4.6), the Commission shall revoke an order made under subsection (4.1) as soon as practicable after the record referred to in the order is filed" — research/sources/gov/ontario-securities-act-extracts.txt Ontario Securities Act s. 127(4.3), ~line 655

questions.stem: A failure-to-file CTO against Ostrander Biotech Inc. has been in effect in Ontario for 120 days. Ostrander now files the missing record. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The Commission must revoke the order on the same day as the filing
options.B: The order cannot be revoked, because it has been in effect over 90 days
options.C: The order ends automatically, because the record is now filed
options.D: The Commission may first require more records if this is in the public interest

questions.rationale: This order is more than 90 days old. So under s. 127(4.6), the Commission may require more records before it revokes the order, if this is in the public interest. Otherwise s. 127(4.3) applies. Revocation is never automatic.
questions.source_quote: "If an order made under subsection (4.1) has been in effect for more than 90 days and the Commission is of the opinion that it would be in the public interest to do so, the Commission may require that, before it revokes the order" — research/sources/gov/ontario-securities-act-extracts.txt Ontario Securities Act s. 127(4.6), ~line 663

questions.stem: The TSX suspends trading in Wexcombe Foods Inc. only because Wexcombe did not pay its listing fees. No regulator issued a CTO. Can a client's order trade on a marketplace?

options.A: No, because UMIR bans every trade while any suspension applies
options.B: Yes, because UMIR 9.1(3) excludes this suspension from the trading ban
options.C: No, until CIRO confirms the suspension in a public notice
options.D: Yes, but only over-the-counter and not on any marketplace

questions.rationale: UMIR 9.1(3)(a) lets an order be entered and trade on a marketplace if the exchange suspended trading only for unpaid listing fees. This is a non-regulatory stop. A CTO or a regulatory halt would ban trading under 9.1(1).
questions.source_quote: "failed to pay to the Exchange or QTRS any fees in respect of the listing or quotation of securities of the issuer" — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR 9.1(3)(a)(ii), ~line 12093

questions.stem: During trading hours, Fernhill Copper Corp. learns that news of its confidential merger talks has leaked. Its share price rises fast. What does NP 51-201 suggest that it do?

options.A: Contact the exchange and ask for a trading halt until it issues a news release
options.B: Wait until the merger is final before it tells the market anything
options.C: Ask its dealer to buy shares to keep the price stable until the close
options.D: Ask the securities regulator to issue a cease trade order on its shares

questions.rationale: NP 51-201 s. 2.3 tells a company with leaked confidential news to contact the exchange and ask for a halt pending a news release. Silence while the price moves on leaked news is not acceptable. A CTO is a regulator's order, not a company disclosure tool.
questions.source_quote: "contacting the relevant exchange and asking that trading be halted pending the issuance of a news release" — research/sources/csa/np-51-201-disclosure-standards.txt NP 51-201 s. 2.3(1), ~line 158

questions.stem: A CTO is in effect against Rothwell Uranium Ltd. Its shares also trade on a foreign organized regulated market. Client Ingrid Solberg wants to sell her shares. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The Participant can sell on the TSX if Ingrid signs a waiver
options.B: The Participant may sell on the foreign market if the CTO's conditions and securities law permit
options.C: No sale is possible anywhere until the regulator revokes the CTO
options.D: The Participant can sell over-the-counter in Canada at a negotiated price

questions.rationale: UMIR 9.1(4)(b) lets a Participant execute a sale on a foreign organized regulated market. The CTO's conditions must be met, and the sale must follow securities legislation. Trades on a Canadian marketplace or over-the-counter stay banned under 9.1(1)(a).
questions.source_quote: "a Participant may execute a sale in the security on a foreign organized regulated market if: (i) all conditions set forth in the order of a securities regulatory authority are met, and (ii) the sale is in accordance with applicable securities legislation." — research/sources/ciro/umir-2026-08-11.txt UMIR 9.1(4)(b), ~line 12105

questions.stem: Regulators issue failure-to-file CTOs to protect the information that investors rely on. According to NP 11-207, what is the main cost of such an order?

options.A: The company must pay a penalty for each day that the order is in effect
options.B: The company loses its status as a reporting issuer at once
options.C: The company's auditor must resign, and the company must appoint a new one
options.D: Existing investors may be unable to sell, and new investors cannot buy

questions.rationale: NP 11-207 s. 7 says that existing investors may be unable to sell, and prospective investors cannot buy, while the CTO is in effect. A CTO is an order that stops trading. It is not a daily penalty, and it does not remove reporting-issuer status.
questions.source_quote: "existing investors may be unable to sell their securities and prospective investors are unable to purchase securities of the issuer while the cease trade order remains in effect" — research/sources/csa/np-11-207-failure-to-file-cease-trade-orders.txt NP 11-207 s. 7, ~line 240

questions.stem: A cap-weighted equity index started at a base value of 1,000. Today its level is 1,250. What does this level show?

options.A: The index contains 1,250 stocks, up from 1,000 at the start
options.B: The average share price in the index is now $1,250
options.C: The market value of the basket rose 25% since the base period
options.D: The index gained 1,250 points since the base period

questions.rationale: An index level is relative to its base value. A level of 1,250 on a base of 1,000 means that the basket's market value rose 25%. The level is not a count of stocks or an average price, and the gain is 250 points.

questions.stem: An index provider adds Kelvington Energy Ltd. to a cap-weighted index and removes another company. Why does the provider adjust the index divisor?

options.A: So that only changes in market prices move the index level
options.B: So that the new constituent gets the same weight as every other stock
options.C: So that the index level returns to its original base value
options.D: So that the index includes the dividends that constituents pay

questions.rationale: The provider adjusts the divisor when constituents change or after a corporate action. Then the substitution itself does not move the index, and only market price changes do. Equal weights and dividend reinvestment are separate design choices.

questions.stem: An ETF tracks a multi-factor index. Which statement best describes how this index differs from a standard cap-weighted index?

options.A: It gives every constituent the same weight and rebalances each quarter
options.B: It weights each constituent by its share price, not its company size
options.C: It holds stocks, bonds and commodities together in one basket
options.D: It selects or weights stocks by traits such as value, momentum or low volatility

questions.rationale: A multi-factor, or smart beta, index selects or weights constituents by traits such as value, size, momentum or low volatility. Market cap alone does not decide. Equal weights and price weights are other weighting methods, not factor methods.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.9 index vs average vs multi-factor

questions.stem: A price-weighted index includes Stock X at $100 and Stock Y at $10. On one day, each stock rises by $1. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Stock X moves the index ten times as much as Stock Y
options.B: Both moves change the index equally, but X's percentage gain is far smaller
options.C: Stock Y moves the index ten times as much as Stock X
options.D: Neither move changes the index, because only market caps count

questions.rationale: In a price-weighted index, a $1 move in a $100 stock moves the index as much as a $1 move in a $10 stock. But $1 is 1% of X and 10% of Y. Market caps matter only in a cap-weighted index.

questions.stem: Founders hold 60% of the shares of Calverley Brewing Corp. as a long-term strategic block. How does a float-adjusted index, such as the S&P/TSX Composite, treat Calverley?

options.A: It uses all shares outstanding, so the founders' block counts in full
options.B: It excludes Calverley, because most of its shares are not available to the public
options.C: It counts only the shares available to the public, so Calverley's weight is lower
options.D: It gives Calverley the same weight as every other constituent

questions.rationale: Float-adjusted indices count only the shares available to the public. They leave out blocks that insiders or strategic holders keep. So Calverley's weight reflects about 40% of its shares, not its full market capitalization.

questions.stem: Client Reuben Castellanos compares a dividend fund with a growth fund that pays no dividends. Which return measure gives a fair comparison?

options.A: Total return, because it includes reinvested dividends as well as price changes
options.B: Price return, because dividends do not change the value of the investment
options.C: Price return, because total return counts the growth fund's gains twice
options.D: Total return, because it removes the effect of price changes

questions.rationale: Total return adds reinvested dividends and interest to price changes. Price return ignores income, so it understates the dividend fund's result. Use total return to compare an investment that pays income with one that does not.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.9 price return vs total return

questions.stem: On one day, a price-weighted index of 30 stocks rises. A cap-weighted index of the same 30 stocks falls. What most likely explains the difference?

options.A: Large-cap stocks rose, while the high-priced stocks fell
options.B: The cap-weighted index reinvested dividends, but the price-weighted one did not
options.C: The price-weighted index uses a float adjustment that the other index does not use
options.D: A high-priced stock with a small market cap rose, while large-cap stocks fell

questions.rationale: In a price-weighted index, high-priced stocks dominate regardless of company size. In a cap-weighted index, the largest companies dominate. So one high-priced, smaller company can lift the price-weighted index while large caps pull the other index down.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.9 exam trap (price-weighted vs cap-weighted)

questions.stem: Which index is an example of an international regional index?

options.A: The S&P/TSX Composite Index
options.B: The MSCI EAFE Index
options.C: A Canadian universe bond index
options.D: An S&P/TSX energy sector index

questions.rationale: MSCI EAFE covers an international region, as MSCI World does. The S&P/TSX Composite is a country index for Canada. A universe bond index is an asset-class index, and an energy index is a sector index.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.9 asset class, sector, country, international

questions.stem: Client Yusra Haddad's target mix is 50% Canadian equity, 20% global equity and 30% bonds. The matching total-return indices gained 9.0%, 12.0% and 1.0%. Her portfolio returned 6.9%. How did it perform?

options.A: It outperformed the blended benchmark by 0.3 percentage points
options.B: It underperformed the Canadian equity index by 2.1 percentage points
options.C: It underperformed the blended benchmark by 0.3 percentage points
options.D: It outperformed the bond index by 5.9 percentage points

questions.rationale: Blended benchmark = 0.50 × 9.0% + 0.20 × 12.0% + 0.30 × 1.0% = 7.2%. Relative return = 6.9% − 7.2% = −0.3 points. A single index ignores her target mix, so it gives a misleading comparison.
questions.qa_note: calc: 0.5*9 + 0.2*12 + 0.3*1 = 7.2; 6.9 - 7.2 = -0.3; distractors: sign error +0.3, vs Canadian equity 6.9-9.0 = -2.1, vs bonds 6.9-1.0 = +5.9

questions.stem: At year-end, RR Oriel Fairbanks sees that his client's portfolio trailed its agreed benchmark. He proposes to use a different index with a lower return in the report. What is the main problem?

options.A: A benchmark must be set before the period, so this change makes the comparison meaningless
options.B: Nothing, because a new benchmark is acceptable if it has the same asset class
options.C: The client must first sign a new account agreement for any benchmark change
options.D: Only the portfolio manager, not the RR, can choose a replacement index

questions.rationale: A good benchmark is specified in advance, before the period starts. If someone changes it after the results, the comparison loses its meaning. A matching asset class does not cure a change made after the results are known.
questions.qa_note: concept: guide 4.10 benchmark properties (specified in advance)

questions.stem: Client Bartholomew Achterberg wants to measure his RR's results against a benchmark. Which property makes sure that the benchmark stands for a real passive choice that he had?

options.A: It is measurable, with returns published for the same periods
options.B: It is investable, so he could have bought it through an index fund
options.C: It is popular, so the media quote it in daily market reports
options.D: It is volatile, so it shows how much risk the RR avoided

questions.rationale: An investable benchmark is one that the client could buy through an index fund. So it is a real alternative, and a gap against it shows real value added or lost. Measurability is also needed, but it does not make the benchmark a real alternative.

questions.stem: Wilhelmina Strand has a Canadian large-cap equity mandate in Canadian dollars. Her RR reports performance against the S&P 500 in U.S. dollars. Why is this benchmark weak?

options.A: It is not investable, because no fund tracks the S&P 500
options.B: It is not measurable, because its returns are not published each period
options.C: It is too broad, because it holds more stocks than her portfolio
options.D: It is not appropriate, because its region and currency differ from the mandate

questions.rationale: An appropriate benchmark matches the mandate's asset class, region, style and currency. A U.S. index in U.S. dollars does not fit a Canadian mandate. The S&P 500 is investable and measurable, so those properties are not the problem.

questions.stem: RR Fenella Okoro writes a weekly market summary for clients. Which sentence follows good practice for a market summary?

options.A: The S&P/TSX Composite price return was +1.4% this week, led by financials after a rate cut.
options.B: Canadian stocks were strong this week, and they will probably keep rising next month.
options.C: Stocks rose about 2% recently, so clients should add more money to their equity positions.
options.D: The index rose this week, and bonds also did well, just as everyone expected.

questions.rationale: A good summary names the index and the period, and it says whether it uses price or total return. It gives the known cause and keeps facts separate from opinion. The other sentences omit the index or period, or they add forecasts or advice.

questions.stem: Client Darius Wexley's 60/40 balanced portfolio returned 5.0%. The equity total-return index gained 9.0%, and the bond total-return index fell 1.0%. Darius says that he trailed equities by 4 points. What is the correct assessment?

options.A: He underperformed by 4.0 points, because equities are his main asset class
options.B: He outperformed by 6.0 points, because the bond index lost money
options.C: He matched the blended benchmark, so his relative return is zero
options.D: He underperformed the blended benchmark by 1.0 percentage point

questions.rationale: Blended benchmark = 0.60 × 9.0% + 0.40 × (−1.0%) = 5.4% − 0.4% = 5.0%. Relative return = 5.0% − 5.0% = 0. A comparison with the equity index alone ignores his 40% bond target.
questions.qa_note: calc: 0.6*9 + 0.4*(-1) = 5.0; 5.0 - 5.0 = 0; distractors: vs equity -4.0, vs bonds +6.0, wrong -1.0

questions.stem: Client Saoirse Lindgren's Canadian equity portfolio had a total return of −3.0% this year. The S&P/TSX Composite total return was −5.0%. How did the portfolio perform against its benchmark?

options.A: It underperformed by 3.0 percentage points, because its return was negative
options.B: It outperformed by 2.0 percentage points, despite its loss
options.C: It underperformed the index by 2.0 percentage points
options.D: It outperformed the index by 8.0 percentage points

questions.rationale: Relative return = portfolio return − benchmark return = −3.0% − (−5.0%) = +2.0 points. A positive relative return shows outperformance, even when the portfolio lost money. The benchmark shows the result of the passive choice.
questions.qa_note: calc: -3.0 - (-5.0) = +2.0; distractors: sign error -2.0, added magnitudes 8.0

questions.stem: Analyst Corwin Eastwood estimates the intrinsic value of Penhallow Brewing Inc. from its statements, management, industry and the economy. Which assumption underlies his method?

options.A: Prices adjust gradually to information, so trends persist
options.B: Statistical relationships in past data will continue
options.C: Prices already reflect all information, so no stock is mispriced
options.D: The market price moves toward intrinsic value over time

questions.rationale: Fundamental analysis estimates intrinsic value, and it assumes that the price moves toward that value over time. Gradual price adjustment and persistent trends are technical assumptions. Continuing statistical relationships are a quantitative assumption.

questions.stem: A dealer's quantitative model buys the stocks with the highest 12-month returns each quarter. What is the main limit of this approach?

options.A: A relationship found in past data can stop working
options.B: It depends heavily on forecasts of future cash flows
options.C: It needs audited financial statements for every stock
options.D: It ignores price history and uses only company news

questions.rationale: A momentum screen is a quantitative tool. It assumes that relationships in past data continue, so its main limit is that a relationship can stop. Dependence on cash-flow forecasts is the main limit of fundamental analysis.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares technical analysts and quantitative analysts?

options.A: Both groups rely mainly on intrinsic-value estimates from company statements
options.B: Technical analysts need financial statements, but quantitative analysts do not
options.C: Technical analysts do not need financial statements, but quantitative analysts may use them
options.D: Quantitative analysts study only charts, while technical analysts run regressions
